name: OpenAI Agents platform
summary: OpenAI's agent stack: the MIT-licensed Agents SDK (agent loop, sessions, handoffs, guardrails, tracing) plus the Responses API, OpenAI-hosted tools (web search, file search, code interpreter, hosted MCP), and a managed Traces dashboard. Execution and hosted tools depend on OpenAI's API; there is no self-hosted control plane.
license: MIT (Agents SDK); platform services are proprietary

agent-runtime.note: The SDK ships a built-in agent loop (Runner) plus Sessions as a persistent working-context memory layer across turns.

orchestration.note: Handoffs and agents-as-tools provide multi-agent delegation; Agent Builder adds a visual multi-step workflow canvas.

knowledge-memory.note: FileSearchTool retrieves from OpenAI-hosted vector stores with managed chunking, embeddings, and hybrid semantic plus keyword search.

tools-integration.note: Function tools with automatic schema generation, hosted tools, and HostedMCPTool for remote MCP servers are built into the SDK.

identity-governance.note: Input, output, and tool guardrails with tripwires plus human-in-the-loop exist, but there is no tenant IAM, per-project authorization, quota policy, or audit log.

observability.note: Tracing is on by default and records model generations, tool calls, handoffs, and guardrail evaluations to the OpenAI Traces dashboard.

data-secrets.note: The Files API and hosted vector stores provide managed file storage, but there is no encrypted secrets manager for agent credentials.

evaluation.note: The Evals API supports JSONL datasets, graders, and eval runs, but it is scheduled to become read-only and then shut down.

channels.note: ChatKit provides an embeddable web chat UI, but no gateways to Slack, WhatsApp, Telegram, or Discord are documented.

code-execution.note: CodeInterpreterTool is a hosted tool that executes model-written code in an OpenAI-managed sandbox.
